name: Chartreuse
lede: Chartreuse is a bright yellow-green named for the liqueur made by Carthusian monks, and on the web it is the full-strength green at hex 7FFF00.

sections.title: A liqueur's name
sections.body: St Clair says chartreuse is named for a French liqueur, the one distilled by Carthusian monks at their monastery of La Grande Chartreuse, and describes it as a pale yellow-green [1]. Paterson also defines it as a pale apple-green with a yellow tinge [2]. Compare [[apple-green]], [[lime]] and [[bright-green]].

sections.title: The web color
sections.body: Paterson notes that the name was adopted by web page creators, and gives the X11 code #7FFF00 [2]. That is a problem for the old word, because #7FFF00 is a fully saturated green-yellow, not a pale one [2][3]. So the books and the web disagree: the old sense is pale, the screen sense is vivid [1][2][3].

sections.title: A vat the same color
sections.body: St Clair uses the word for indigo dyeing: fabric dipped into the chartreuse-hued vat turns from yellowish green to sea green on contact with air, then settles on a deep blue [4]. The word there names the cloth's first color out of the vat, a passing stage, since the finished cloth ends as [[indigo]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive tool could not compute a match count for this swatch, so no painting statistics are quoted [3]. The swatch is at the limit of what a screen can show [3].
